Three npm artifacts: static review, 2026-10-26

Judgments: all three supplied specimens are BENIGN on the balance of their
actual code, packaging, behavior and recovered provenance. No deployment
context, installed dependency lockfile, or original external-source diagnostic
was supplied. A malicious application could use these libraries; that is not
established for these specimens. Registry identity was corroboration, not a
substitute for tracing code. No package, install hook or downloaded code ran.

Original SHA-256 identities

@toptal/picasso-utils 3.1.0:

posthog-js 1.433.2:
197d0c48ccfe7af5893a6c74126aaa4b74782de2516d34b9847488b4cff984be

Each specimen is byte-identical to its exact-version tarball independently
retrieved by forager from registry.npmjs.org. The apparent unscoped Picasso
filename is a collection name; its manifest and bytes identify the genuine
scoped package. A renamed collection file is not evidence of impersonation.
Original archives, recovered artifacts and .forage.json provenance remain in
session scratch/bad-analysis; sample files themselves were not modified.

Method
Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md first. Ran atomscan --no-update --analyze local
--mode slow --format json --follow=none on all three original full paths,
and cleave facts on each archive. Extracted all ordinary members, refusing
traversal and special files. Also dumped full source facts for Nx's updater,
native loader, graph runtime and hasher and PostHog's capture, consent, storage,
request, script loader and replay implementation. Inspected actual code paths,
including minified/transpiled bundles and their readable lib/src counterparts.
Inspected all 45 Picasso distributed JavaScript modules.

Followed dependency/reference leads with atomscan, then fetched 61 distinct
original direct dependency/optional-native/selected-peer tarballs with forager
and scanned their members: 45 for Nx, seven for Picasso, nine for PostHog.
There were 62 fetch requests because the PostHog web-vitals npm alias points
at the same exact release. Exact declarations were fetched as written; ranges
were investigated at their declared lower bound. These are explicit controls,
not a reconstruction of an unknown machine's installed dependency resolution.
Inspected sensitive dependency behavior, including node-machine-id's OS ID
queries and SHA-256 transformation and ap-style-title-case's text transform.
Native optional dependencies were scanned with disassembly; no specimen code
was executed. Those dependency scans had no hostile or suspicious findings;
the verdict does not use that absence as evidence of intent.

Nx 19.5.1
The main executable is the Nx monorepo build/task CLI. postinstall imports its
workspace graph/native components, checks that this is the root Nx package and
nx.json exists, stops an existing workspace daemon, computes project graphs,
and verifies/updates Nx Cloud only when configured. The native loader copies
specific Nx platform modules to its versioned cache to avoid file locks and
restores Module._load after loading; this is native integration, not an implant.
The sole new Function source is webpack's constant 'return this' global lookup.

GitHub release support resolves GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN, gh hosts.yml oauth_token,
or 'gh auth token' to authenticate normal api.github.com release requests.
Package-manager helpers copy .npmrc and other configuration into temporary
package workspaces so installs can resolve private packages. These are real
credential-related/configuration operations in their declared developer-tool
workflow, not evidence of credential theft. Build shell execution, background
daemon IPC, platform selection, hashing and module loading remain detected.

The formerly trojan-filed async timers actually perform requested daemon
shutdown and batched graph recomputation. '--no-interactive' belongs to normal
Nx generators and cloud-connect commands, with no AI-agent inference. A
remote_plugin source identifier names plugin infrastructure without proving
remote process creation. Their matchers and notable criticality are retained
at precise neutral homes.

Forager also retrieved https://cloud.nx.app/nx-cloud/client/verify, which
advertised version 2610.22.0068 at /nx-cloud/static/client-bundle. Retrieved,
extracted and inspected that gzip bundle. It implements cache/task runners,
authenticated cloud requests, worker processes and CI/self-healing support.
Decoded its JavaScript hex escapes for static reading. Its obfuscated variable
names are an accurate suspicious observation, retained unchanged in the scan.
Its current server response is not evidence of the historical bundle served
to a 2024 installation, or of a machine's custom NX_CLOUD_API configuration.

Picasso Utils 3.1.0
The package exports React hooks, formatting/string/color helpers, modal stack
management, transitions and DOM layout helpers. The prepublishOnly hook runs
the TypeScript build; no install-time payload is present. unsafeErrorLog simply
logs to console; it is not an exception-stealing uploader. Mouse listeners
update component state, intervals invoke supplied callbacks, IntersectionObserver
tracks visibility, and modal/page locking temporarily sets html.style.overflow
to 'clip' and restores the prior value when its last layer disappears. These
behaviors fit the published UI utility purpose. No network or command-execution
path was found in its distributed modules. Runtime/peer imports lead to normal
UI modules and text transforms, not a concealed stage.

Extended the existing overflow operation to cover document-root/descendant
assignments and CSS 'clip', preserving the existing document.body/'hidden'
variant. This adds three notable member/container findings to Picasso; a read
of style.overflow and an ordinary object with an overflow field do not match.

PostHog JS 1.433.2
This is the browser analytics and session replay SDK. init/capture construct
application-configured event records, queue/batch/compress them, and dispatch
via fetch/XHR/sendBeacon to configured API hosts. Defaults use us.i.posthog.com.
Feature flags, surveys, toolbar/site-app extensions and recorder scripts are
loaded through the configured request router. disable_external_dependency_loading
and preparation hooks control that script loading. Storage records analytics
identifiers and consent; input listeners and DOM snapshots serve replay and
autocapture. Explicit ph-no-capture/ph-sensitive exclusions, password masking
and default replay maskAllInputs=true are implemented. ConsentManager checks
stored consent, opt_out_capturing_by_default and optionally DNT/GPC; the default
is not universal opt-in-only capture. These controls and documented tracking
purpose explain the behavior without inventing consent in an unknown deployment.

Base64/UTF-8 conversions and gzip are data/transport/rrweb serialization, not
concealed script evaluation. The two formerly trojan-filed Buffer conversions
occur in rrweb code; their supported final default UTF-8 conversion is now a
notable micro-behavior. Existing Base64 detections remain unchanged.
Fetched https://us-assets.i.posthog.com/static/1.433.2/recorder.js: it is
byte-identical to the specimen's dist/recorder.js (SHA-256
73e4897739cb4a755a0e340e72c2ce2a2d326dfa21e74a3468b3bb1036000e5c).
No additional execution stage was found there.

Rule placement and retained attack coverage
* Async callback: objectives/supply-chain/hidden-payload/trojan to
  micro-behaviors/time/schedule/timeout::async-arrow-callback, same matcher.
* Default UTF-8 conversion of a Base64 buffer: former trojan base64-decode-call
  to micro-behaviors/data/decode/utf8::base64-buffer-default-text. The shorter
  identifier character class preserves every former ASCII identifier and also
  accepts Unicode word characters. The Base64 directory's existing observations
  are untouched; there is no score-motivated duplication or demotion.
* Newsletter target/FOLLOW context: retained verbatim at
  micro-behaviors/communications/messaging/channel. Description states the
  actual target/selector context rather than asserting that a query ran.
* The covert-channel-follow attack composite retains all three required roles,
  16-line proximity, file scope and hostile criticality, at the social channel
  manipulation home. It does not establish payload concealment. Its description
  states co-occurrence instead of claiming a proven data-flow relation.
* Generic no-interactive option to process/argument/option; remote plugin-stage
  vocabulary to metadata/lang/source/naming/resource. Updated exact consumers.
* To keep coherent leaves within their reviewed budgets, relocated the existing
  certutil DLL-path reference into fs/path/library and generic registrationId
  vocabulary into metadata/lang/source/naming/resource, preserving scope,
  matchers, exclusions and criticality. Updated the sideload and WhatsApp
  credential consumers. Neither an argument option nor a generic registrationId
  proves process creation or a WhatsApp protocol operation.
* Broadened/renamed the overflow operation and updated its iframe consumer.

Audited exact and ancestor-directory consumers. Removing option/name vocabulary
from the process/create selector corrects the unsupported claim that those
strings alone establish a launch. Explicit attack consumers retain the same
signals via their new canonical IDs. No hostile/suspicious sample finding was
removed, narrowed or demoted. The nine executable regression controls cover
all moved primitives, the retained newsletter composite, explicit-follow and
timer-only near misses, overflow reads, and pre-existing agent-destruction and
encoded-invite-follow hostile fixtures outside this batch. The option's prior
test-harness exclusion is preserved: controls are copied outside testdata paths
while checking its positive. All nine passed. New hostile composite precision
is 4.8, above the authoring bar; fixture behavior, not that score, establishes
retained coverage.

Before/after
comparison.json records full counts and classifier scores. All supplied
archives AND every analyzed member have zero hostile and zero suspicious traits
before and after. Nx: 727 analyzed units, notable instances 3265 -> 3265.
Picasso: 261 units, notable 528 -> 531. PostHog: 810 units, notable 7569 -> 7569.
These totals include propagated container findings. All lost IDs in the sample
comparisons are the documented relocations; no material attack coverage loss.
Classifier level remains -1 (benign) for every sample. Scores:
Nx 0.6263297 -> 0.6263297; Picasso 0.51853627 -> 0.51853627;
PostHog 0.48781294 -> 0.6146059. No classifier/verdict disagreement remains.
The engine reported an older feature-spec/model revision and flow analysis
limits in some large or complex bundled sources. Readable member sources were
inspected to mitigate those gaps; static inspection cannot prove runtime safety
or validate future mutable URLs and dependency resolutions.

External source labels
The supplied hostile labels are not supported by the inspected code. Broad
heuristics for install hooks, download/load/update behavior and build execution
could flag Nx, and analytics/input/DOM capture could flag PostHog. Picasso's
scoped identity may also have been lost in collection or package attribution.
Those are plausible explanations, not recovered facts about the source's exact
signature or labeling decision. No diagnostic from that source was available.
Purpose-consistent execution paths plus independently recovered identical
packages tip all three judgments to BENIGN.
